newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CCB TO FLOAT UP TO 29.5 PCT IN IPO.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CCB TO FLOAT UP TO 29.5 PCT IN IPO.

text.p: Belgium's second largest bank, Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet said on Monday it would issue up to 29.5 percent of its capital in an initial public offering starting on November 4.
At a news conference, CCB chief executive Francois Narmon also confirmed that the bank had sold an additional five percent to Belgian insurance company SMAP/OMOB.
The IPO is an integral part of CCB's plan to form a cross-border alliance with Credit Local de France (CLF), which is already listed in Paris.
CCB said the price of the offering would be determined by a bookbuilding process, running from November 4 to 15 for institutional investors and from November 8 to 15 for retail investors.
The price at which the shares will be offered to the public will be indicated on November 8, CCB said in a statement.
The final price will be communicated on November 20, it said.
"This price will be based largely on the price of CLF holding shares on the Paris stock exchange, after having taken into account the likely impact of a payment of an exceptional dividend," CCB said.
CLF has said it would pay an exceptional dividend to its shareholders before the alliance went into effect.
CCB has applied to list 12.67 million shares starting on November 20 under the name Dexia -- the name CCB and CLF have given to their cross-border group.
